issue: Does the First Step Act's amendment to the § 924(c) stacking penalty (§ 403(a)) apply when a defendant whose pre-Act sentence was vacated is resentenced after a remand?

sides.position: The First Step Act's § 924(c) stacking amendment applies at resentencing after a remand, because a vacated pre-Act sentence is a legal nullity (the excerpt names only the Fourth Circuit as holding this).
cases: United States v. Bethea, 841 F. App'x 544 (4th Cir. 2021)

sides.position: The First Step Act's § 924(c) stacking amendment does not apply at resentencing after a remand. The excerpt says courts are split but does not name the circuits on this side, so no circuits are identified.

quote: While various courts of appeals are split on whether § 403(a) applies at resentencing following a remand, they are unanimous in holding that “First Step Act § 403 does not extend to defendants who were sentenced prior to the Act’s enactment but ha[ve] not yet exhausted their direct appeals.”
cite: United States v. Waite, 12 F.4th 204 (2d Cir. 2021)
